A water district representative will attend the October 12th Howard Street meeting to restate the district's position.

minutes.summary: The water district commissioners approved option three for a PFAS pilot study and approved the warrant for an October 19 special meeting to vote on funding. Staff presented rising electric and chemical costs and rate options, but the rate decision was deferred to the next meeting pending comparison with other towns. The superintendent also reported on a truck bid, SCADA, Howard Street, and Emerald Place billing.

what_happened.line: The water district commissioners approved option three for the PFAS pilot study by voice vote; the count was not audible.
The board approved the warrant for a special meeting on October 19 at 6 pm, moved from the 12th because of a ZBA meeting.
The pilot study is to be paid from an account already saved for system enhancement and connections, so no new request goes to residents.
A decision on a water rate increase was deferred to the October 12 meeting, after a member calls other towns for comparisons.
Staff said electric and chemical costs are running above budget, leaving a gap that rates would have to cover.

why_it_matters: Water customers face a likely rate increase, with a decision now expected in October or early November, and the options raise the first usage tier.
The October 19 special meeting is where residents are asked to vote on funding for the PFAS work.
